definitions.palace: the 3x3 fortress where the general and advisors stay
definitions.river: the middle line that elephants cannot cross

beginner.guidance: Prefer everyday words. Use Xiangqi piece names (general, chariot, horse, cannon, elephant, advisor, soldier) not chess names. At most one short term from allowed_terms if it helps.

definitions.cannon screen: a piece the cannon needs to jump over to attack or capture
definitions.blocked horse: the horse cannot jump because the adjacent 'leg' square is occupied
definitions.central file: the middle file (e) that often controls the palace
definitions.fork: one piece attacks two targets at once
definitions.hanging: a piece is unprotected and can be taken

intermediate.guidance: Use club-level Xiangqi vocabulary from allowed_terms when accurate. Say chariot/cannon/horse — not rook/knight. Brief definitions optional if a term might confuse.

definitions.facing generals: both generals on the same open file — illegal if nothing blocks between them
definitions.blocked elephant: the elephant cannot move because the eye (midpoint) square is occupied
definitions.palace pressure: attacking or infiltrating the opponent's 3x3 fortress
definitions.prophylaxis: preventing the opponent's plan before it happens
definitions.conversion: turning an advantage into a concrete win

advanced.guidance: Technical Xiangqi terms from allowed_terms are welcome when precise. Do not use chess-only jargon (castling, en passant, zwischenzug). Stay accurate and concise.
